the embryonic endothelial cell progenitors (EPCs) are a distinct subset of EPCs and that they have a specific recruitment pattern to tumors that is mediated by the selectins and their ligands.

The main takeaway from our work is that

embryonic endothelial precursor cells (EPCs), which are present in embryonic development and are also present in the adult, have the capacity to contribute to neovascularization and tumor angiogenesis.

eEPCs, which were previously thought to be committed to the endothelial lineage and thus to be unable to differentiate into hematopoietic cells, retain their potential to differentiate into blood cells in the adult.
